Today, Apple celebrated the opening of its Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, Texas, and here are the relevant details.

Apple will provide training for business leaders at its new Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston

Apple today opened its new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized enterprises, giving them hands-on access to the most advanced equipment, interactive labs, and a variety of tools to accelerate innovation. The Advanced Manufacturing Center is located within the same Houston facility that is responsible for producing and shipping Apple's advanced AI servers and will begin production of the Mac mini within this year. […] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: 'In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We have built the plant, begun production, and have already shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers from the factory. Today we are delighted to open this brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which will be a place where business leaders, workers, and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple's most groundbreaking products. We also look forward to beginning production of the Mac mini later this year. We believe in the strength of American workers and American creativity, and we are moving forward at an astonishing pace, because what we want to create is not just good products—what we want to build is the future of American manufacturing.'

Tim Cook announced his Houston trip via social media, making a special trip to attend the opening event. Guests attending the launch ceremony included U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Congressman Christian Menefee, and Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis.

The Advanced Manufacturing Center covers an area of 20,000 square feet, and Apple's experts will "directly share their knowledge with participating businesses and entrepreneurs, helping accelerate the development of American smart manufacturing."

The first batch of business leaders arrived today to attend the inaugural training session. The day's topics centered on smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
